title: Capfolder 0.1.4: see who owns what, and when

posts.label: Post
posts.text:
How much of your equity has vested?

It's a simple question. Answering it usually means opening a spreadsheet and doing some math by hand.

So Capfolder 0.1.4 puts it on one screen:

1. A Vesting screen. The option pool at a glance: total, granted, vested, still available. A row per grant. Open one and you see its graph: the cliff, the monthly steps, today, and where vesting stops if someone leaves.
2. A person page you can read in five seconds. Vested, next vest and fully vested, right next to the name.
3. An import check. Moving from Pulley, Carta or Cake? Type in the old tool's totals and Capfolder checks them to the share. A grant with more vested than granted blocks the import.
4. "What needs my attention?" Up to 3 things to do next, each with a Take me there button. It works with no AI connected.

One honest limit: the import check compares totals, not every row, so you still check a few people by hand.

Capfolder is free, open source, and keeps your cap table in a folder on your own computer.

Founders: when someone on your team asks how much of theirs has vested, how do you answer today?

posts.label: Post
posts.text:
I'm building Capfolder, an open-source cap table app. A cap table answers "who owns what?". It took me a while to notice that founders and employees almost never ask that. They ask "how much of mine has vested, and when is the rest mine?"

Until this release, Capfolder answered that one holding at a time. You clicked into a row and read the math. Correct, but slow, and nobody does it.

What we did

Version 0.1.4 puts the time question first:

  1. A Vesting screen. The option pool at a glance (total, granted, vested, available), and a row per grant that opens to its graph: the cliff, the monthly steps, today, and where vesting stops if someone leaves.
  2. A person page you can read in five seconds. Vested, next vest and fully vested sit next to the name. The graph is on the left, the holding and its history on the right.
  3. An import check. Coming from Pulley, Carta or Cake? Type in the old tool's totals and Capfolder checks them to the share.
  4. "What needs my attention?" Up to 3 things to do next, each with a Take me there button.

The lesson: put the answer where the question starts

The numbers on the new screens aren't new. The engine already worked out every vest, to the share. What changed is where they show up: next to the name, before you click anything.

Two things I'd do again:

  • One engine, many screens. The Vesting screen, the person page and the Excel export all draw from the same vesting math. A screen can't drift from the others, because none of them does its own math.
  • Ship the useful part without the fancy part. "What needs my attention?" sounds like an AI feature. It isn't: it's a short list built from the app's own list of missing documents and open signatures. It works with no AI connected, which is how most people will first meet it.

What I don't know yet

Whether people find the Vesting tab without being told. Your cap table never leaves your computer, so I can't watch: I'll learn from people telling me. And the import check compares totals, not every row, so you still check a few people by hand.

The full write-up, with screenshots: https://capfolder.com/blog/see-your-vesting/

What's the question your users ask that your product answers too slowly?

posts.label: Article
posts.text:
Originally published on capfolder.com.

Capfolder is an open-source (AGPL) cap table app built with Tauri and React. Your cap table lives in a folder of plain files on your own computer: an append-only, hash-chained events.jsonl in the Open Cap Format, plus your signed PDFs.

0.1.4 is about time: who owns what, and when. Here's how the pieces fit, in very little new math.

1. One vesting engine, every screen

The vesting math already existed: the golden tests check it to the share. The new Vesting screen, the person page and the Excel export's Overview and Vesting by month tabs all read from that one engine. None of them does its own math, so they can't disagree.

The graph shows the cliff, the monthly steps (or a straight line), today, and where vesting stops when someone leaves. The 409A price behind "vested value" is stored as an OCF VALUATION, not a setting.

2. The person page

Vested, next vest and fully vested moved next to the name. The graph went left, the holding and its history right, stacking on narrow windows. Y-axis labels got short (40K, 4M), which fixed labels being cut off.

3. Checking an import to the share

The last import step puts each total next to a box for the old tool's number. Fully diluted is required; each class, options outstanding, pool available, SAFE total and stakeholders are optional. If the file has a vested-so-far column, each grant is checked against our own schedule as of the export date:

const ours = vested === null ? null : vestedAt(qty, terms.get(key)!.data, start, p.exportDate).vested;
// 1 share of rounding allowed (tools round months differently)

More vested than granted blocks the import outright.

4. "What needs my attention?" without a model

Ask AI routes this one question to plain code before any model is called:

const ATTENTION = /needs? (my )?attention|what('s| is) urgent|what should i do/i;
// in askChat:
if (ATTENTION.test(question)) return attention(d);

attention() takes open and signed-but-not-wired envelopes, then the What's missing gaps (red first, grouped by kind), and keeps at most 3. Each Take me there target passes a whitelist: only certain screens, a person who exists, a row id that's a holding, a plan or an envelope.

5. A date bug

"As of" was set once, when the app opened. Leave it open overnight and a SAFE signed today was hidden behind yesterday's date. Now it follows the calendar (the founder's local day, not UTC) until you pick a date yourself.

What it doesn't do yet

The import check compares totals, not every row. The Before you cancel checklist asks you to check 3 people by hand.

The code is on GitHub. If you've built an app where several screens show the same numbers, how do you keep them from drifting apart?

What it doesn't do yet: the import check compares totals, not every row, so you still check a few people by hand.

A bug from Capfolder 0.1.4 worth knowing about: Ask AI crashed, but only in newer Chrome-based engines (Windows' WebView2).

Scrolling to the latest answer returned a value there, and our React effect passed it straight back. React took that return value for a cleanup function and crashed when it tried to call it.

Lesson: in useEffect, don't let an arrow function implicitly return whatever the call gives you. Use braces.

The rest of 0.1.4: https://capfolder.com/blog/see-your-vesting/?ref=dailydev

posts.text:
Capfolder is an AGPL-3.0 desktop app (Tauri + React) for startup cap tables. The design rule: the folder is the source of truth.

• events.jsonl: an append-only, hash-chained log of Open Cap Format (OCF) records. Mistakes are fixed with new entries, never edits.
• captable.csv: regenerated on every change, opens without the app.
• docs/: your signed PDFs, linked to the holdings they prove.

0.1.4 adds vesting: a Vesting screen, a person page and Excel tabs, all reading one vesting engine that golden tests check to the share.

Moving off Pulley before Dec 8? Export the cap table and every signed doc first.

Capfolder (free, open source) imports the export and checks the totals against Pulley's to the share, before saving: https://capfolder.com/migrate/from-pulley/
posts.tips: Search 'Pulley shutting down' / 'Pulley alternative' (Live). Reply only where someone asks where to move. Copy, then tweak to their question. Mark each reply you send as its own box (+ Reply under this).
